name: How do I know if my shower needs to be completely replaced or just repaired?

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my shower needs to be completely replaced or just repaired?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start by determining whether the problem is cosmetic or structural. Loose grout, cracked caulk, or a damaged door may need a focused repair, while movement, recurring moisture, soft walls, staining outside the enclosure, or persistent leaks can indicate that the waterproofing assembly should be opened and assessed. Context: A shower replacement is more involved than changing a fixture because demolition may reveal damaged framing, substrate, plumbing, or flooring. Elite Remodeling & Design can review the existing bathroom as part of its broader bathroom remodeling and design-build process. Key factors: leak location; wall and floor condition; shower size; valve placement; and whether plumbing must move. Practical guidance: Photograph stains, peeling materials, and the valve area before requesting estimates, and ask each contractor to explain the likely cause rather than pricing only visible finishes. A replacement plan is usually more dependable when hidden conditions and final materials are addressed together.
acceptedAnswer.description: Replace the shower when leaks, soft materials, movement, recurring moisture, or failed waterproofing suggest a deeper problem. Minor grout, caulk, or hardware damage may only need repair. Have the enclosure and surrounding walls inspected before choosing, because demolition can reveal plumbing, framing, or substrate issues.
